idiom_name: static final poison object on a BlockingQueue
implementation_notes: BlockingQueue has no close or shutdown operation - the JDK's own documentation recommends special end-of-stream or poison objects for exactly this purpose. Put a distinguished instance (static final Object POISON = new Object(), or a reserved enum in a typed queue) once per consumer after the last work item; consumers block in take() and exit on identity or enum comparison. When the consumers are tasks in an ExecutorService, its shutdown()/awaitTermination() cycle (or the AutoCloseable close()) is the framework's own drain-and-stop, so no sentinel is needed. Note that BlockingQueue rejects null, so null cannot serve as the pill.
pitfalls: null cannot be enqueued (BlockingQueue throws NullPointerException), so a null pill fails at the producer, not at the consumer.
A single shared pill instance is dequeued by exactly one consumer; posting fewer pills than consumers leaves workers blocked in take() forever.
take() throws InterruptedException on interrupt or shutdownNow; catching it without restoring the interrupt flag hides the stop request.
Adding pills while other producers still offer work breaks the drain ordering; stop production first, or let ExecutorService.shutdown() own the drain.
